title: OKR capacity fungibility and initiative credit allocator
creator: Priya Nambiar
description:
Problem: As Redwood grows, product and platform teams commit to company-level OKRs that require pooled engineering capacity across multiple orgs (Runtime, Console, Dedicated). Current planning treats capacity as fixed per-team, causing brittle rollups, underutilized reserve pockets, and last-minute scope cuts when priority shifts.

Objective: Define a lightweight operational model and tooling pattern — 'capacity fungibility' and an 'initiative credit allocator' — that lets PMs and Eng teams safely exchange committed capacity, reserve capacity, and initiative credits across cross-functional initiatives while preserving SLA and SLO commitments. The model should enable predictable OKR delivery without over-allocating headcount or freezing feature lanes prematurely.

This ticket scopes the PM-side playbook, acceptance criteria, stakeholder contracts, and the initial MVP metadata model for the allocator. Engineering work (runtime autoscale behavior, quota APIs) will be spun into downstream ENG tickets after alignment sessions.
acceptance_criteria: A clear definition and taxonomy of capacity types (committed, fungible reserve, opportunistic burst, credit-backed transfer) documented and approved by Eng leads and Finance
A one-page operational runbook for initiating a capacity transfer between teams, including handoff checklist and rollback criteria
A lightweight metadata model (CSV/JSON schema) to represent initiative credits and transfers that can be ingested by Dashboards and capacity planners
Playbook includes escalation paths, minimum notice windows, and SLA guardrails to protect latency/cost objectives
Pilot agreement signed with 2 cross-functional initiatives (one Runtime-led, one Console-led) to trial the allocator within a single quarter
A dashboard slice in the Console showing current credit balances, pending transfers, and forecasted utilization for pilot teams
deliverables: Taxonomy doc (Confluence): capacity types and trade-offs
Two internal kickoff workshops recorded and notes published
Post-pilot retro and decision: expand / iterate / retire
stakeholders: PM leads: Priya Nambiar, Marco Silva
ENG leads: Asha Patel (Runtime), Daniel Wu (Console)
timeline: Week 1–2: taxonomy and runbook draft; Week 3: stakeholder review and schema finalization; Week 4: pilot kickoff with two initiatives; Weeks 5–8: monitor pilot, implement dashboard view; Week 9: retro and recommendation for Q2 rollout
risks: Overly permissive transfers could erode SLA headroom and increase latency/cost incidents
Finance and revenue recognition rules might limit how credits can be allocated across cost centers
Insufficient instrumentation could lead to disputes over actual consumed capacity
Teams may game the system if incentive alignment is not clarified
decisions: Use conservative minimum notice window of 10 business days for committed-capacity transfers during pilot
Credits are time-boxed to the originating quarter by default and require explicit approval for cross-quarter rollover
All transfers must include an explicit SLO impact statement approved by owning SRE lead
